change: a lesson or unit switch now settles what is under it, so a teacher's click actually opens the assignment
_context: Reported 2026-09-09: '1.2 have the lock off but it isn't open.'
The assignments board has said 'a mixed switch settles everything under it
OPEN on the first click' since it shipped. It was not true. The route wrote
ONE row at the clicked scope, narrower rows survived, and narrower always
wins at read time.
So a teacher whose lab carried its own closing row flipped the 1.2 lesson
switch to open, the lab stayed shut, the board correctly re-rendered mixed,
and clicking again did exactly nothing. Reproduced before touching anything:
after closing the lab at activity scope   LOCKED (explicit-closed)
after opening the whole LESSON            LOCKED (explicit-closed)
rows: [1.2|*|1, 1.2|terminal-lab|0]
A switch that cannot settle is worse than a missing one, because there is no
way to tell from the outside that it is not working. She had no move that
would have fixed it except finding the individual chip.
THE RULE IS CONTAINMENT, NOT WIDTH, and that is the whole risk in the fix. A
lesson row (1.2, *) and an activity-type row (*, quiz) overlap without either
containing the other, so clearing one for the other throws away a setting the
teacher never spoke about. A width-based implementation is the obvious wrong
way to write this and passes every test that only exercises the unit case, so
it is mutated explicitly.
PINNING SURVIVES. Close the unit, then open one lesson inside it: the narrow
write clears nothing above itself and still wins. That is the case the ladder
was built for and it is asserted end to end, not by reading rows.

checks.name: the reported click works, containment holds, pinning survives, the delete stays in its lane
checks._why: Section 1 reproduces the teacher's exact sequence through the LAB route, because routes/quiz.js will never serve a lab and the first draft of this suite checked the wrong door. Section 4 is the worst outcome available from this change: a delete that reaches another class or another unit.

checks.name: the ladder itself is unchanged
checks._why: This changes what is STORED, not how it resolves, so the assertions that pin precedence, both enforcement paths and the gradebook's view of a lock must be untouched. One assertion in it DID move and it is worth knowing why: four sequential writes ending on the unit-activity scope used to leave four rows, and now the last one correctly settles the activity row under it. Reordered widest-first rather than relaxed, with both behaviours recorded in the comment, and a new assertion added that the settling happens in the other order.

checks.name: an independent containment rule agrees with the route on every write shape
checks._why: Written from the rule in English rather than from the DELETE's WHERE clause, which would be one implementation wearing two hats. The matrix is exhaustive over the four scope shapes in both positions, so the two pairs that catch a width-based implementation are covered by construction rather than by remembering to add them. It also asserts the matrix both clears and keeps rows, because a comparison where nothing is ever cleared proves nothing.

checks.name: THE ONE THAT SHIPPED: write the row and clear nothing
checks._why: This is the exact state the route was in when the report arrived. It must go red on the assertion that names the teacher's own click.

checks.name: the delete forgets the unit, so it reaches across the whole course
checks._why: The worst outcome available here. A teacher settling one unit would silently wipe her settings in every other unit of the same course, and nothing in the response or the board would say so.

checks.name: the delete forgets the class, so it reaches every teacher
checks._why: The other direction of the same blast radius, and the one that would take out somebody else's class entirely. Asserted with a bystander class holding a row at the identical location.

checks.name: the rederive's containment rule goes width-based
checks._why: Pins the comparison to containment rather than to the open/locked counts. If the second implementation drifts to a width number the diff stops being a second opinion, and it would drift silently because the unit and assignment cases agree either way.
